newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia crude steady to soft, remains cautious on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Asia crude steady to soft, remains cautious on Iraq.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady to soft on Thursday but remained nervous over the volatile situation in Iraq especially following news that rival Kurdish factions clashed in northern Iraq, traders said. But Asia's benchmark Tapis crude firmed.

According to latest reports heavy fighting took place near a strategic bridge at the village of Degala as Iraqi government troops stood by. The November Brent/Dubai spread was quoted at $1.80/$1.90 compared with an offer Wednesday at $2.20. The Dubai intermonth spreads narrowed to 35/43 cents for Nov/Dec compared with 42/46 cents Wednesday, with Dec/Jan at 35/42 cents.

MidEast market was actively traded Wednesday with 450,000 barrels of October Qatar Land done at plus eight cents a barrel between two US majors. A US major bought 250,000 barrels of October Murban crude at plus 11 cents from a French firm, while 500,000 barrels of Oman for October was traded at plus three cents between two majors. Oman was offered at plus five cents.
Traders said a major, a Japanese trader and a regional refiner still hs October Oman to offer while a trader and a Europen refiner has October Dubai.
Malaysia's Petronas hiked August Tapis price by 33 cents to $21.19 and raised September premium for term sales to 40 cents.

Tapis rose after 600,000 barrels for October were sold to a US refiner at plus 70 cents, 10 cents over its last deal. Seller has an end-September Tapis cargo reserved for Burma but would offer it for October if not committed. The seller is offering at 80 cents but sellers deemed this too high. Seller also sold 200,000 barrels of October Labuan at $22.10 to a refiner. After being absent in August, China imported 1.5 million barrels of September Minas between ICP minus 15-22 cents. China also bought 1.2 million barrels of September Bach Ho. Traders said 400,000 barrels of September Minas was available.--Ramthan Hussain, Singapore, (+65 870 3084), J. Oshima, Tokyo (+813 5473-3708)
